meta.title: Who really said "I lost an arm on my last trip home. My left arm"? | Quotle.info
meta.description: These are the opening words of Octavia E. Butler’s Kindred (1979), spoken by its fictional narrator Dana. They do not describe an injury to Butler herself.

author.name: Octavia E. Butler
author.heading: About Octavia E. Butler
author.bio: Octavia E. Butler brought questions about hierarchy, survival and interdependence into speculative fiction. Her books include Kindred and the Parable novels, and she received a MacArthur fellowship in 1995; her essays also address the practical work of becoming a writer.

context.heading: Why it mattered
lead: The prologue reveals Dana’s injury before readers learn how it happened. That opening turns the story into a question about what returning from the slaveholding past costs her, giving physical consequences to a time-travel narrative.

schema.faqAnswer: Yes. Octavia E. Butler wrote these opening words for Dana, the fictional narrator of Kindred; they are not an autobiographical statement by Butler.
schema.verdictNote: Verified as fictional narration written by Butler.
